prompt: Compare the three storage methods described in this project's sources in a table. For each cell, point to the source it comes from or mark it as your inference.

documents.title: Method note: B-tree
documents.text:
# B-tree store
Measured on the reference device: p99 point-read latency 2.1 ms; 9,000 writes per second sustained. Write amplification was not measured.

documents.title: Method note: LSM tree
documents.text:
# LSM-tree store
Measured on the reference device: 38,000 writes per second sustained; write amplification about 11; p99 point-read latency 3.4 ms.

documents.title: Method note: append-only log
documents.text:
# Append-only log store
Measured on the reference device: 52,000 writes per second sustained. Requires periodic compaction. Read latency has not been measured yet.

truth: From the sources: B-tree: 2.1 ms p99 point-read latency, 9,000 writes/s, write amplification not reported. LSM tree: 38,000 writes/s, write amplification about 11, p99 point-read 3.4 ms. Append-only log: 52,000 writes/s, needs compaction; read latency NOT reported and write amplification NOT reported. A good table attributes each figure to its source, marks missing values as not reported (rather than inventing them), and labels any inference.
